rows.evidence: Q1: Section 2 - two-year field experiment (2005, 2006) in Bursa, Turkey with five drip-irrigation deficit treatments in a randomized complete block design, three replications. Q2: Section 3.5 and Fig. 7 - the authors report a polynomial relationship between WUE and seasonal mean CWSI (R2 = 0.67, RMSE = 0.03) and state that the highest WUE could be obtained at a CWSI close to 0.6; Section 3.3 and Table 3 show WUE peaking in T25 (0.63 and 0.56 kg m-3). Q4: Section 2 and Section 3.5/Fig. 7 - ETc was measured by soil water balance with neutron probe readings to 120 cm, canopy temperature by infrared thermometer, and the authors report a power relationship between ETc and mean CWSI (R2 = 0.99) plus the yield-ETc relationship (Fig. 1), i.e. the stress-transpiration-ETc pathway linking CWSI to WUE is measured. Q8: Section 3.1 - measured ETc for non-stressed plots exceeded FAO-56 estimates and the authors admit they cannot define sources such as variety, growing period and sub-surface flows, and that evaporation from wetted soil after irrigation was probably higher; Section 3.4 - VPD range (1-4 kPa) narrower than recommended for baselines and some CWSI values fell below 0 or above 1; Section 3.3 - the highest-WUE schedule (T25) causes about 27.5% yield loss; Conclusion - threshold applies to the conditions described in this study and the drip method.
rows.notes: The passage reproduces the study's own statement almost verbatim. Caveats: irrigation was actually scheduled on soil water depletion replenishment, and CWSI was computed post hoc and related to WUE; CWSI was not itself used to trigger irrigation. The review label 'app_scheduling' is broader than the infrared-thermometry CWSI scheduling tested here; no app was involved, but the technology (CWSI-based scheduling) is what the passage describes, so no mismatch flagged. Q3 no: WUE-CWSI relationship rests on a single regression of one data set. Q5 no: one site, one soil, one cultivar, two years. Q6 no: 23.4 m2 plots. Q7 no: the authors say the high-WUE strategy could be preferred under water scarcity or high water cost, but this is a condition for adopting the strategy, not a stated requirement for the effect; the locally derived baseline requirement is cited from Nielsen (1990), not their own finding. Q9 no: only RMSE and R2 for the regression and LSD for yield; no SD, SE, CI or uncertainty analysis for WUE or the CWSI optimum.
